labels.landing: I built this to see Jung’s whole field in one place: every archetype, symbol and instance he wrote about, set where and when it appeared and cited to the page. Everything in it connects back to one centre, which Jung called the Self. That’s where it starts.
labels.lensAion: Jung’s history of the aeons, Pisces to Aquarius.
labels.lensAstrology: Your birth sky beside Jung’s, read through the corpus.
labels.readingTagline: Jung’s history of the aeons — the precession of the equinoxes through Pisces into Aquarius, read on the Earth.
labels.skyClockLede: Where the spring equinox lies among the stars is a calculation, and it depends on how the zodiac is drawn. These are the sky’s own boundaries under stated conventions, set beside Jung’s months, which stay as the reading gives them. Nothing here is a forecast.
labels.skyClockFishes: The two fishes are Jung’s division of Pisces; no astronomical convention divides it.
labels.astrologyIntro: Enter a birthday and you get a walk through that sky, planet by planet, with what Jung and Kathleen Burt wrote about each planet and sign. Jung’s own chart is here as the first one, so you can read yours beside his.
labels.astrologySun: Every walk here ends at the Sun, and Jung reads the sun as a symbol of the self. So whoever’s chart it is, the line runs to the same centre.
labels.astrologyOtherTies: Links the atlas draws, not Jung
labels.astrologyOtherTiesOnly: Links the atlas draws (Jung gives none)
labels.astrologyCharts: Jung’s chart and your birth form
labels.quaternityLink: Jung’s four: the elements, the functions
labels.coincidencesFraming: Jung on what counts, and on runs of chance
labels.dreamsIntro: Write a dream down. The images in it that the field knows are picked out; each one opens onto the dreams and visions in the corpus that carry the same image. That is how Jung read a dream: by lining it up with its parallels.
labels.symbolsIntro: Name a symbol and see how it runs through the field: what Jung said it is, every dated instance of it, the dreams and visions it turns up in, and what it expresses.
labels.symbolsNone: It holds the images Jung wrote about, under the names his texts use.
labels.amplifyDreams: The dreams and visions in the corpus where this image appears: the parallels Jung lined up beside a dream image.
labels.amplifyNoDefinition: Jung gives no definition of this image in the vault’s records.
labels.redbookLede: Each vision of the book, and what it became in Jung’s later work.
labels.birthFraming: the sky at that moment, read in Jung’s keys
labels.birthLimits: It states where the Sun, Moon and planets stood and links each to what Jung wrote of it. It makes no forecast and passes no verdict on a person.
